resolutions.researcher_notes: Official Egyptian Presidency 'National Projects' page, listed under Presidential Inaugurations, filed under Petroleum & Natural Gas, dated October 2019: 'Construction of a pipeline to transport oil produced from the Southwest Mleiha fields to the oil treatment station in the Mleiha area, estimated at about 7,000 barrels/day, at a cost of $31 million' -- an official inauguration entry, which by context confirms the pipeline is built and operating (status inferred, per rule 8, not a literal 'operating' token). Single source -> medium, independent=false.

The Egyptian Presidency's official inauguration page for this pipeline is dated October 2019, not 2020 (values: StartYear1=2020). Per rule 7, a source giving a different value from the sheet is not cited as support; flagging the disagreement rather than forcing a match. No other dated source was found for the pipeline's start.

No source found giving a length figure for this pipeline (130 km). The presidency.eg inauguration page gives capacity (~7,000 bbl/d) and cost ($31M) but not length; the other seed citations (alwafd.news, offshore/hydrocarbons-technology.com) do not mention a pipeline length either.
No source found giving a diameter figure (10 in) for this pipeline. None of the seed citations or the presidency.eg page mention pipe diameter.

This article (the seed hydrocarbons-technology.com URL now 301-redirects here, same publisher/rebrand) states Eni pursues its Western Desert exploration strategy 'through AGIBA, a joint venture between Eni and Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC),' operating in the Meleiha concession where the Southwest Mleiha field sits -- supports Operator=Agiba Petroleum ('عجيبة للبترول'). The seed alwafd.news article (Agiba raising Southwest Mleiha field production) would corroborate this directly but is blocked (403, confirmed live 2026-08-27) with no Wayback capture available, so it could not be read; single usable source -> medium, independent=false.

Same article: 'In the Meleiha concession, Eni holds a 38% interest through its subsidiary Ieoc while Lukoil and EGPC respectively hold 12% and 50% stakes' -- corroborates EGPC and Eni SpA (via Ieoc) as owners/partners in the Meleiha concession that this field/pipeline sits in, consistent with Owner1=EGPC / Owner2=Eni SpA (no percentages are staged, so I am not proposing the article's percentages as values, only citing it as support for the two named owners; Lukoil's 12% stake is also in the article but is not a sheet value here). Single source -> medium, independent=false.
